1	# 0004. Defer full type-checker integration
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-07-22 (retroactive)
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	OXC's structural, no-type-checking approach (`0001`) can't resolve conditional types, mapped types over an unbound generic, or a few `@emotion/styled`-specific call shapes — these need real type inference. TypeScript 7 is now a stable native compiler and LSP language service, but a stable programmatic contract for the per-node facts this project needs is still a separate question.
8	
9	## Decision
10	
11	Don't integrate a type checker now. Every gap that would need one degrades to a `Diagnostic` plus an `Opaque` prop type instead of a wrong answer, and gets tracked in `docs/rdt-coverage.md`'s "Known gaps summary" table. Revisit when either a stable public programmatic API or the TypeScript 7 LSP can supply the required facts and passes the accuracy, lifecycle, and cost gates in `docs/type-checker-integration.md`.
12	
13	## Consequences
14	
15	- A real, bounded set of real-world types (see `docs/type-checker-integration.md` for the current list) shows up as `Opaque` in extraction output until this changes.
16	- No dependency on an unstable, fast-moving API in the meantime.
17	- The eventual semantic process/client stays outside `crates/core`; core retains an owned-data enrichment contract and no I/O/async responsibility.
18	- The gap list needs to stay current in `docs/type-checker-integration.md` and `docs/rdt-coverage.md` as new patterns get found — otherwise this ADR quietly goes stale.

content.text:
**Yes, it's enough to plan tsgo support, but not enough to commit to an implementation.** The 7.1 beta on Oct 6 is the point where you can test against a pinned public release. That's the gate your `docs/type-checker-integration.md` already sets.

**7.1 plan** ([iteration plan](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/63703))
- Beta is Oct 6, RC is Nov 10, and stable is Nov 24, 2026.
- 7.0 shipped without an API. The team says 7.1 will ship "a new (and different) API" ([7.0 announcement](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-0/)).
- `@typescript/typescript6` provides the TS 6 API side by side in the meantime.

**What the 7.1 API roadmap covers** ([#4830](https://github.com/microsoft/typescript-go/issues/4830))
- The roadmap lists content mappers (Vue/Svelte/Astro), LSP middleware, `createProgram(options)`, `createSourceFile`, `transpileModule`, `parseCommandLine`, solution builder, transformers, `formatDiagnostics`, VFS overlays, and `NodeHandle<T>`.
- It says nothing about checker queries, transport, non-JS clients, or stability guarantees. It only lists remaining work, so checker queries are probably already built, but I couldn't confirm that.

**What already exists on typescript-go `main`** (from [`internal/api/proto.go`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/typescript-go/main/internal/api/proto.go), read through a page summarizer, so it isn't verified against source)
- It has `GetTypeAtLocation`, `GetTypeOfSymbol`, `GetContextualType`, `GetResolvedSignature`, `TypeToString` and `GetAliasTypeArguments`.
- It has conditional-type accessors for the check, extends, true and false types, plus type-parameter, constraint and index-info queries.
- That maps well onto the four operations in your doc: generic substitution, conditional types, mapped/indexed types, and `typeof`.
- It looks better suited than LSP hover, which probably can't give the expanded type shape. Route 1 (the programmatic API) is more promising than your doc assumes.

**Risks**
- The API is on `main` and unpinned, and the team says 7.1's will be "different". Don't name methods in a spec yet.
- I found only a JS client. It's unclear whether a Rust client can talk to it directly. The alternatives are a Node sidecar, or a submodule-plus-shim like [tsgolint](https://github.com/oxc-project/tsgolint), which vendors typescript-go rather than using a published API.
- `crates/cli/config.rs` already shells out to Node. A Node sidecar using the 7.1 JS client would keep `crates/core` I/O-free and fit that pattern. This is my inference, not something the plan states.

**What you can do before Oct 6, independent of route**
1. Freeze fixtures for each deferred type class, and build the oracle from the `@typescript/typescript6` checker.
2. Write the owned-data enrichment contract in core.
3. Spike a Rust or Node client against a pinned `@typescript/native-preview` build to see whether the checker API is reachable at all.

`docs/type-checker-integration.md` (verified 2026-09-11) doesn't mention the 7.1 plan or dates. Want me to update it and ADR 0004 with these facts?

This package provides a preview build of [the native port of TypeScript](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/typescript-native-port/).

content.text:
**7.1 is developed on `microsoft/TypeScript` `main` (`version = "7.1.0-dev"`), not typescript-go.** typescript-go is closed: its README says "This Repo Is Closed… continue development in the original repo", and it will be archived in September. It has a `ts7-release` branch, but there is no `release-7.1` branch yet. The API code is in `tsc/internal/api/` (Go) and `packages/typescript/src/api/` (JS client). I cloned `main` to the scratchpad and read it.

My earlier `proto.go` reading came from the frozen typescript-go copy, so treat it as superseded.

**Implementation**
- `tsc --api` takes `--cwd`, `--pipe`, `--callbacks`, `--async`, `--timing` and `--runExternalCode`.
- It talks over stdio or a named pipe/unix socket. The default is a custom msgpack tuple, `[type, method, payload]`. `--async` switches to plain JSON-RPC.
- The msgpack mode has no request IDs, so it's strictly serial. JSON-RPC is the easier target for a Rust client.
- The model is snapshot-based: `createSnapshot`/`createProgram` return snapshot and project handles, and every query takes `(snapshot, project, …)`. `--callbacks` lets the client serve file contents.
- There are 157 methods, including `batchRequests`.
- The checker surface covers all four operations from your doc:
  - **Generics:** `getTypeAtPosition`, `getResolvedSignature`, `getTypeArguments`, `getAliasTypeArguments`.
  - **Conditional types:** `getCheckTypeOfType`, `getExtendsTypeOfType`, `getTrueTypeOfConditionalType`, `getFalseTypeOfConditionalType`.
  - **Mapped/indexed types:** `getPropertiesOfType`, `getIndexInfosOfType`, `getApparentPropertiesOfType`.
  - **`typeof`:** `getTypeAtLocation`, `getAliasedSymbol`.
  - Also `typeToString`, `getJsDocTags` and `getConstantValue`.
- `TypeResponse` has no mapped-type fields. You only get a mapped type's resolved properties, so unresolved generic mapped types stay opaque, same as with tsc.

**Stability**
- The JS API is exported only under `typescript/unstable/*`.
- There were about 20 API commits in the last month, several of them breaking:
  - `updateSnapshot` was replaced on Sep 17.
  - Typed project IDs landed on Sep 18.
  - `compilerOptions` moved to the top level of the `createProgram` params on Sep 18.
- Open PRs are still changing the surface: module-resolution overrides (#64299), sync connections to existing servers (#64175), wasip1 (#64174), and a build orchestrator API (#64158).
- `initialize` returns only `useCaseSensitiveFileNames` and `currentDirectory`, so there is no version handshake. We'd pin an exact `tsc` build and check its version at startup.
- The checker method names mirror TS 6, so that part should settle sooner than the snapshot and program surface.

**Clients**
- The only client is the JS one.
- The Go API is `internal/`, so we can't import it.
- I found no cgo, NAPI or c-shared code on `main`.

**Unknowns for the spike**

updated 2026-09-03T20:54:29Z
These are the categories of remaining API features I think we need for 7.1, with a few specific items included below. Costs are very rough estimates and hopefully skew high.

This list does not include non-feature work like bug fixes, performance improvements, or docs, which are all important too.

## 1. TS Server Plugin Replacements

### 1A. Content mappers

- PR: microsoft/typescript-go#4712
- Needed by: Vue, Svelte, Astro, MDX, etc. Angular?
- Remaining cost: 3 dev-weeks

### 1B. LSP client middleware registration

TS Server plugins have the ability to directly modify LS requests/responses. Existing TS 7 LSP/API integration only allows extensions to add TS-augmented providers, and cannot filter/modify any stock responses or alter the TS 7 editor behavior in any way. Our extension can expose a command or cross-extension API allowing other extensions to register callbacks that we can invoke in middleware in vscode-languageclient. (This is not a very well documented feature of the client, but it exists.)

- Needed by: Angular (diagnostic filtering), Svelte, likely others
- Cost: 1 dev-week

## 2. Top-level utility APIs

Currently, almost all APIs require obtaining a snapshot containing a full program build of the project/files being worked on. This is a pretty good model for working within a tsconfig-defined project on disk, especially if needing to update the project over time, but awkward for many kinds of ad-hoc analysis; it’s not a natural substitute for `ts.createProgram` much less `ts.createSourceFile`.

This list is not exhaustive, but these are the top priority ones people have asked for.

### 2A. `createProgram(options)`

This will still be backed by a snapshot, but provides the opportunity to specify `rootFiles` and `compilerOptions` instead of needing to resolve a tsconfig file from disk. On the server side, I'm not sure whether the snapshot should be derived from an existing snapshot or should be built entirely from scratch. Either way, it should be an idempotent operation (other open projects not included in the returned snapshot, new snapshot not adopted by the project session). We’ll need to expose the underlying Project somehow (`program.project` parent pointer seems fine) and make the returned Program disposable (disposing its snapshot, since this API will guarantee 1:1 mapping between Program and Snapshot).

Note: This dovetails with 3B and may be better suited to be folded into that.

- Needed by: likely ts-morph, many others
- Cost: 1 dev-week

### 2B. `createSourceFile(fileName, sourceText, options)`, `createSourceFileFromFile(fileName, options)`

Quick way to get an isolated AST from text or disk. Open question as to whether this can be truly stateless, or should be server-tracked to allow for a follow-up `bindSourceFile`, but the latter could be added in a backward-compatible way if needed. May be better to introduce a parameter indicating whether to send binder symbols back in the same response.

- Needed by: ts-blank-space, likely ts-morph, many others
- Cost: <1 dev-week

### 2C. `transpileModule(sourceText, options)`, `transpileModuleFromFile(fileName, options)`, `transpileDeclaration(sourceText, options)`, `transpileDeclarationFromFile(fileName, options)`

Quick way to transpile TypeScript code to JavaScript or declaration files without needing a full program or project context.

- Needed by: ts-loader, TypeScript playground
- Already in progress by @andrewbranch
- Cost: <1 dev-week

## 3. CLI-wrapper APIs

We’ve discussed high-level APIs that would make it easy (or at least possible) to create a CLI tool that performs similar functions to `tsc`, with modifications that can only be achieved through API usage. Some of the scenarios motivating this will be handled by content mappers (#4712) instead, but I think Angular is still interested in this.

I’m treating `--watch` functionality as out of scope for now, because the TS 6 public API didn’t provide watching.

### 3A. `parseCommandLine` and related functions

High priority:

- `parseCommandLine(commandLine: readonly string[])`
- `readConfigFile`
- `parseJsonConfigFileContent(json, { configDirectory } | { configFileName })` 

Lower priority: other non-@internal exported functions from commandLineParser.ts that have equivalents in Go

- Needed by: Google
- Cost: <1 dev-week

### 3B. Solution builder APIs, `createIncrementalProgram`

Budgeting more time for this because the API is built on top of the LSP server’s project layer, which currently does not integrate with the solution builder whatsoever. It may turn out to be simple, but it's a new integration point into a complex system.

- Needed by: ts-loader, Bloomberg, Angular?
- Cost: 2 dev-weeks

### 3C. Custom transformers

Much of the reason to create a CLI wrapper is making emit modifications. I think we can support an API very similar to Strada here by fetching the JS emit as a SourceFile (AST), running custom transformations client-side, and sending the transformed AST back to the server for final emit (basically `printNode`). I think the infrastructure to do this already exists, but may be missing a lot of emit-node metadata required to do proper comment preservation and formatting.

- Needed by: Angular, Google, ts-loader
- Cost: 2 dev-weeks (less for MVP)

### 3D. `ts.formatDiagnostics`, `ts.formatDiagnosticsWithColorAndContext`

`formatDiagnostics` can likely be a pure client-side port from Strada. The complication with `formatDiagnosticsWithColorAndContext` is that the source file text needed to create the context may or may not already be cached on the client. Having `formatDiagnosticsWithColorAndContext` be a dedicated remote API call probably makes sense.

- Cost: <1 dev-week

## 4. General infrastructure

### 4A. VFS and overlay improvements

The included VFS implementation was meant only for testing, and includes no caching. There should be a way for the API client to provide file system contents eagerly and prevent IPC round-trips. This is easy implementation-wise, but finding the right design (particularly around invalidation, passthrough to disk, interaction with LSP-connected API) is important.

- Needed by: Bloomberg, TypeScript playground
- Cost: 1 dev-week

### 4B. Generic `NodeHandle<T>` and type guards on node handles

`NodeHandle` is currently non-generic, but would often be useful to carry narrowing information. A `symbol.valueDeclaration.resolve()` yields a `Node` when it could be a `Declaration` instead. This is easy, but also allowing a `NodeHandle<Node>` to be narrowed to a more specific `NodeHandle` type was surprisingly hard without code duplication or hacks. The likely path forward is giving in to code duplication or hacks and just getting it done.

- Needed by: everyone
- Cost: minimal for MVP

## 5. Additional methods in existing categories

There are still additional methods that can be exposed with no new concepts or infrastructure. The biggest categories are language service methods and small top-level utilities. The hardest part is just identifying them.

content.text:
**Recommendation:** don't go through our NAPI. Have Rust spawn `tsc --api` and speak its protocol directly, in an optional crate that the CLI and the binding both use. It's viable now, but the primary query has to be per-component, not per-`Opaque` leaf. Nothing in the repo was changed; the scratch clones and probes are in the scratchpad.

## Current state
- **Nightlies:** `typescript@next` is `7.1.0-dev.20260920.1` and includes the API, so no Go build is needed. `@typescript/native-preview` is stale (last published July 7).
- **Breaking redesign:** the snapshot redesign ([#64154](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/64154)) landed Sep 17–18 and broke `updateSnapshot`, project IDs and `createProgram` params.
- **Open PRs:** none touch the checker read methods we'd use.
  - [#64299](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/pull/64299) adds module-resolution overrides.
  - [#64158](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/pull/64158) adds the build orchestrator.
  - [#64175](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/pull/64175) adds sync connections via FIFOs.
  - [#64174](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/pull/64174) adds a wasip1 build, labelled experimental with "no warranty".
- **Perf caveat:** a ts-loader benchmark on the roadmap issue shows the new API up to about 43% slower than TS 6 on check-heavy flows on an M2. The maintainer said they can't look at perf until after the beta.

## Design finding
The current doc models enrichment as replacing `Opaque` leaves. The benchmarks say otherwise: 10 components account for 2,696 of the 2,720 missing props, and six of them fail before any `Opaque` leaf exists. Ariakit, ark-ui, fluentui and storybook-emotion fail on generic-alias substitution and leave `composes` empty.

So the primary request should be a component-level props query. I verified this works: a virtual overlay file containing `React.ComponentProps<typeof Button>`, passed through `createSnapshot({ fileSystem: { kind: 'layer', … } })`, returned all 292 props. Against real MUI Button types the same query returned 314 props. This is also what react-docgen-typescript does, so it should reach exact parity. Leaf-level enrichment becomes secondary.

## Interface options
| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Rust spawns `tsc --api --async` (JSON-RPC, Content-Length framing) and speaks the protocol | **Recommended.** No Node in the loop, and it works from the CLI and the addon alike. The async server handles requests concurrently. |
| Through our NAPI, calling the JS API | Reject. The binding has never called into JS (no `ThreadsafeFunction`), the CLI has no Node, and core is sync/rayon. |
| Node sidecar, like `config.rs` | Fallback. It absorbs protocol churn but adds a hop and a Node dependency. |
| In-process (cgo, wasm) | Not available on `main`. |

Under the recommendation, NAPI only carries the option that turns the backend on. `resolve_complex_types` is already plumbed through the binding and nothing reads it. The addon's Rust code spawns and reaps the `tsc` child itself.

Positions are UTF-16 code units, which I confirmed: a UTF-8 byte offset returned the wrong type. OXC gives UTF-8 byte offsets, so we need a conversion. `ComponentMapping` already has spans, but `Opaque` leaves have none, so leaf-level enrichment would need extractor changes.

## Performance
These are my measurements through the Node client, 3 rounds on small fixtures. A Rust client skips the JS hop, so these should be upper bounds.

| Measure | Result |
|---|---|
| Spawn + first snapshot | 33–72 ms (the first run is the slowest) |
| First check, MUI or 300 files | 1–15 ms |
| Sequential request round trip | ~0.1 ms |
| 500 positions in one batched request | ~1 ms |
| MUI Button walk (314 props, one `typeToString` per prop) | 34–41 ms (316 requests) |
| tsc server memory | ~100 MB RSS |
| Layer an overlay-file update | 0.4 ms (program rebuild deferred, not measured) |

Against our baseline of 50 ms for the whole 21-library corpus, ~20 ms per fixture and 1.75–2.1 ms incremental, tsgo would dominate runtime whenever it's on. Off by default is the right call.

The addressable set is small: about 10 components, so roughly 60 ms fixed plus about 0.4 s worst case if queried naively. That figure is derived, not measured. The `batchRequests` method should cut the per-property cost, but I haven't measured it.

## Proposed shape
- **Core:** an owned-data component request and result, hooked in after Phase 4/5 and also in `WatchSession::update_file`. Plugin hooks don't fire on incremental updates today, so this is the sibling-path trap your CLAUDE.md warns about.
- **New feature-gated crate:** owns the child process, JSON-RPC client, timeouts and supervision. `config.rs` has no timeout or reaping today. Blocking `std::process` plus one reader thread is enough. Core needs no tokio.
- **Version pinning:** the protocol has no version handshake, so pin an exact `typescript` build and check `--version` at startup.

## Unverified
- **Rust client:** I haven't run one, and I read the Go transport code but never exercised the raw protocol.
- **Real projects:** I tested explicit root files, not a tsconfig-based project with paths and jsx settings.
- **Watch mode:** the cost of rebuilding the program after an update is unmeasured.
- **Stability:** protocol drift is likely until the beta.

Next step: a Rust JSON-RPC probe against the 10 outlier fixtures, measuring prop parity with react-docgen-typescript. Want me to build it, or first update the type-checker doc and ADR 0004 to the component-level model?
Is there a way to limit the cost of tsc to just what we need?

content.text:
**Yes to both.** You can trim what tsc does per run, and a fast Rust result followed by tsc enrichment is the better shape, because it hides most of the cost that can't be trimmed.

## What trims the cost
The API uses one persistent, lazily-checking checker. It never computes diagnostics or emits unless asked, so checker-count options don't apply. The cost is parsing and binding the reachable files, plus the types we actually query.

I ran the MUI Button query, 5 rounds each, medians:

| Config | Wall | CPU | RSS |
|---|---|---|---|
| base | 85 ms | 270 ms | 102 MB |
| `types: []` | 79 ms | 260 ms | 100 MB |
| `GOGC=off` (+ `types: []`) | 71 ms | 200 ms | 111 MB |
| `GOMAXPROCS=2` | 114 ms | 160 ms | 99 MB |
| `GOMAXPROCS=1` | 220 ms | 160 ms | 95 MB |
| `singleThreaded` compiler option | 144 ms | 160 ms | 99 MB |
| +300 unrelated root files | 88 ms | 320 ms | 112 MB |

- **`GOGC=off`** helps for a short-lived process. It gives the best wall time and about 25% less CPU, for +9 MB. I haven't tested it with a `GOMEMLIMIT` safety net.
- **`GOMAXPROCS`** trades wall time for CPU. It's the safer knob, since `singleThreaded` is flagged internal and could disappear.
- **Root files:** pass only the component files plus our overlay, not the tsconfig `include`. Unrelated roots add CPU because parse and bind aren't lazy. Take the tsconfig's options but not its file list.
- **`types: []`** made little difference here (only three `@types` packages installed) but is safe, since imports still resolve. It should matter more in repos with many `@types`.
- **Batch requests:** the 500-position batch took about 1 ms, against about 0.1 ms per sequential request.

Differences under about 10 ms are noise. This is one fixture through the Node client.

**Not trimmable:** parsing `lib.dom` and the reachable `.d.ts` graph. That floor is about 70–85 ms wall and 200–270 ms CPU at MUI scale, with no cross-process cache. Only two things avoid it: not spawning when nothing is degraded, and keeping the process warm in watch mode.

## Fast Rust result first, tsc after
This fits our structure:
- **Overlap the spawn.** Start `tsc` and `createSnapshot` at Phase 0 while the roughly 20–50 ms Rust extraction runs. By the time we know which components degraded, tsc is usually warm.
- **Pull, not push, at the binding.** Keep `extract_file_incremental` as the fast path and add a second async call such as `enrich_component(session, file)`. The vite plugin applies the result when it resolves. This needs no `ThreadsafeFunction`, which the binding has never used.
- **CLI:** the default is the fast result only. An opt-in flag waits for enrichment. I'd leave flag names to the spec.
- **Content-bound results:** tag each enrichment with the file hash and drop it if the file changed. This is the "stale response" gate from your doc.
- **Only query degraded components.** `CollectedType::needs_type_checker()` exists and is never called.

**Gap:** six of the ten outlier components degrade silently. Generic-alias substitution leaves `composes` empty with no diagnostic, which conflicts with non-negotiable #6. They need a diagnostic anyway, and that diagnostic becomes the enrichment trigger.

Want me to write this up in `docs/type-checker-integration.md` and ADR 0004, or start with the Rust probe?
How do we include the diagnostic so we can trigger enrichment from tsc?

**We don't need to add a diagnostic.** The current source already emits them. What's missing is which component each one belongs to.

**Correction:** last turn I said six of the ten outlier components degrade silently. I took that from `docs/benchmarks.md` and my own run of `target/release`, which is from Jul 25 and predates several resolver fixes. With the current build (`target/debug`, Aug 23), every outlier fixture emits diagnostics:

| Fixture | Diagnostics |
|---|---|
| ariakit | 6 `OPAQUE_TYPE`, 3 `MAX_DEPTH_EXCEEDED`, 1 `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` |
| fluentui | 3 `OPAQUE_TYPE`, 1 `GENERIC_ARGUMENT_MISMATCH`, 1 `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` |
| headlessui | 8 `OPAQUE_TYPE`, 7 `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT`, 4 `SKIPPED_CANDIDATE` |

ark-ui, storybook-emotion and base-ui show the same pattern. The docs should be corrected.

## Why the diagnostics can't be the trigger as they are
- **Attribution is lost:** `resolve_component` returns `(ComponentEntry, Vec<Diagnostic>)`, so each component's diagnostics are still paired with it in Phase 5. Then `diagnostics.extend(diags)` at `pipeline/mod.rs` flattens them into one list.
- **No component identity:** `Diagnostic` has `file`, `line` and `column`, with no component field. `line` and `column` are always `None`. `file` is often not the component's file. For example, ariakit's `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` points into `@types/react`. Filtering the global list by file would misattribute.
- **Public contract:** `Diagnostic` is a public serde struct, so I'd leave it alone.
- **Codes are too coarse:** `OPAQUE_TYPE` covers both real gaps and by-design opaques like `SxProps` and `ModuleAugmentation`.

## Proposal
1. **New `EnrichmentHint`** in `types/`, `pub` and `#[non_exhaustive]`, following the `rust-types` checklist. It holds the component's file, its export name, and a set of degradation reasons.
2. **Record reasons at emission time.** Add `state.degrade(reason)` on `ResolveState` next to the existing `diagnostics.push` sites: conditional, mapped, indexed access, template literal, depth exceeded, generic mismatch, and unresolved import. `CollectedType::needs_type_checker()` already exists at `collected.rs:117` and is never called, so it can be the predicate. This is more precise than classifying by code, and the diagnostic stays the user-facing signal.
3. **Keep hints Rust-side.** They go on `ExtractionOutput` as `#[serde(skip)]`, so the JSON and the snapshots don't change. The NAPI `enrich_component` call reads them from session state.
4. **Both paths.** `WatchSession::update_file` has the same resolve step, so it must produce the same hints. Add a test asserting exact hint sets from `extract()` and `update_file()` on one fixture, per your sibling-path parity rule.

## Open questions
- **Export info:** the overlay query needs `import { X } from './file'`, so the hint needs the export name and whether it's a default export. I haven't checked whether `ComponentMapping` carries that. Non-exported components can't use the overlay route.
- **Panic stubs:** the empty stub that Phase 4 creates on a panic could also be enriched by tsc. Whether it should is a policy decision.
- **Ghost entry:** every fixture output contains a 0-prop `PureComponent` entry. I didn't investigate it, but it would trigger spuriously if it isn't filtered.

result.output:
# 0005. Contain panics at a single, per-item boundary

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-08-05

## Context

There was no `catch_unwind` anywhere in the repo. Panic safety existed only by accident: `extract_all`, `extract_file_incremental`, and `initialize_session` happened to run inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`, whose `JoinError` catches an unwind as a side effect of tokio's own plumbing, not a decision anyone made. `pipeline/mod.rs`'s rayon `.map()` closures had no per-item boundary, `plugin.rs` called each `DocgenPlugin` hook with zero isolation between plugins, `create_session`/`close_session` skipped `spawn_blocking` entirely and got no protection at all, and `watch.rs`'s `std::sync::Mutex` could poison permanently as a direct consequence of an unprotected panic happening while the lock was held.

## Decision

Panics reachable from a rayon `.map()`, a `DocgenPlugin` hook, or a NAPI entry point are caught at `crates/core/src/panic_guard.rs`'s `pub fn contain_panic<T>(label: &str, f: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> Result<T, Diagnostic>`, converting the payload into a `Diagnostic` tagged `DiagnosticCode::InternalPanic` instead of aborting a batch, killing the whole pipeline, or poisoning a lock. `contain_panic` wraps its closure in `AssertUnwindSafe` internally, so callers never reason about `UnwindSafe` themselves — this matters because the plugin-hook call sites pass `&mut SourceData`/`&mut ComponentEntry`, and `&mut T` is unconditionally `!UnwindSafe` in std. The internal `AssertUnwindSafe` is justified by this codebase's data shape: `SourceData` and `ComponentEntry` have no interior mutability (`Cell`/`RefCell`) that could leave a torn, observable half-write behind a caught panic — the whole per-item operation is what gets abandoned, not a partial mutation trusted afterward.

`contain_panic` wraps the rayon parse-phase and resolve-phase closure bodies in `pipeline/mod.rs`, each individual `plugin.on_x(...)` call inside `PluginRegistry::run_on_file_extracted`/`run_on_component_resolved` in `plugin.rs` (not the whole loop, so one bad plugin degrades only itself), and all five NAPI entry points in `crates/binding/src/lib.rs`. `watch.rs`'s poisoned-lock `.expect()` was also replaced with `.unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())` as defense in depth.

## Consequences

- One bad file, plugin, or session call degrades to a diagnostic instead of taking down its batch, the pipeline, or the session.
- `PluginRegistry::run_on_file_extracted` and `run_on_component_resolved` changed their return type from `()` to `Vec<Diagnostic>` to carry caught-panic diagnostics back to the pipeline — a real API change, not just internal wiring.
- `extract_all`, `extract_file_incremental`, and `initialize_session` were already panic-safe via `spawn_blocking`'s `JoinError`; wrapping their bodies in `contain_panic` makes that guarantee documented and consistent with the rest of the codebase rather than incidental. `create_session` and `close_session` were genuinely unprotected before this and are now wrapped directly.
- `watch.rs`'s `std::sync::Mutex` poisoning is now defense-in-depth rather than a live risk — panics upstream (rayon batches, plugin hooks) are contained before they'd reach that lock while held.
- Every future concurrent, plugin, or FFI entry point has one obvious place to route through instead of re-deriving the answer.

## Alternatives considered

napi-rs (the pinned version) has its own opt-in `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` attribute that wraps a function body in `catch_unwind` at the FFI boundary. It would work for the five NAPI entry points, but we used `contain_panic` explicitly there too, for one mechanism across rayon, plugins, and FFI instead of two.

content.text:
**Rethink:** the tsgo API can run react-docgen-typescript's own algorithm, so the semantic backend should be a second resolver reconciled with the structural one, not an enrichment patch. I ran RDT 2.4.0 against a clone of its algorithm on the tsgo nightly (`7.1.0-dev.20260920.1`), with the same options the validation harness uses. Everything below was measured in the scratchpad, and nothing in the repo changed.

## RDT's model, from its source
- **Unit:** module exports whose type has a call signature (parameter named `props`, or the only parameter) or a construct signature with `props`.
- **Props:** apparent properties, plus every union constituent's.
- **Type string:** `typeToString(baseConstraint ?? type)` with default flags.
- **`parent` and `declarations`:** the declaration's parent interface or type alias.
- **Description:** JSDoc plus tags.
- **Defaults:** read from the AST, not the checker.
- **Filter:** drops `children` without a doc comment.

## Parity measured
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| 13 components in 11 files, including the 10 outliers | 0 missing, 0 extra props; `required` matches on 100% |
| Descriptions (ariakit, MUI, fluentui, shadcn) | 294/294, 311/311, 288/288, 292/292 |
| `parent` on ariakit MenuButton | 294/294, 12 requests |
| Whole corpus (55 files, one program) | 70 common components, prop counts equal on 70/70 |
| Corpus cost | 385 ms (tsgo, including spawn) vs 955 ms (RDT in-process) |
| Class components (synthetic file, since the corpus has none) | K=2 and Q=3, matching RDT |

Of the corpus's 26 RDT-only entries, 23 have zero props (enum members, type aliases, hooks) because RDT emits any JSDoc'd export. The other 3 are real components under a different default-export name. I confirmed the name match for mui `Button` (311/311), not for antd `Button` or mui `TextField`.

**Type strings:** identical apart from two things.
- **Union order:** tsgo prints members in checker-id order, so it differs from TS 5.9 and RDT's own order isn't stable across versions. After sorting members, the shortfall drops from 271 of 294 (ariakit) to 294/294.
- **RDT's `.replace(' | undefined','')` runs twice:** it strips a nested `=> string | undefined` to `=> string`, losing information. Canonical output shouldn't copy that.

Copying RDT's base-constraint step took headlessui from 4/234 to 234/234.

## Architecture
1. **Two resolvers, one output shape.** The structural resolver stays the default: offline, about 50 ms for the whole 21-library corpus. The semantic one is opt-in and follows RDT's algorithm. When it finds a component, it is authoritative for props, types, `required` and `parent`. Structural still supplies defaults, non-exported components, and the fallback.
2. **Hints reduce to a file path.** Trigger a semantic pass for files containing degraded components. That solves the panic-stub and export questions, since `mapping.file_path` exists even for stubs. It drops the overlay text, UTF-16 offsets, binding names and leaf-level enrichment. The overlay trick from last turn is demoted to a fallback for non-exported components.
3. **Diagnostics belong to a component's result.** On semantic success, the degrade diagnostics for that component should be superseded. Today Phase 5 flattens them (`diagnostics.extend(diags)`), so attribution is lost.
4. **Freshness contract:**
   - I edited a dependency file and told tsc about it (`fileNotifications.changed`). The dependent component's props updated: 0.5 ms for the update, 2.8 ms for the query.
   - As a negative control, an un-notified disk edit stayed stale.
   - So `update_file` must notify tsc on every change, with a parity test, the same class as your 2026-08-12 stale-watch bug.
5. **Types are structured, not just strings.** MUI's `variant` walks to `"contained" | "outlined" | "text"` through the module augmentation. The structural path emits `ModuleAugmentation` opaque for that. The backend crate needs a Type-to-`PropType` adapter. `SxProps`, `HtmlAttributes` and the `known.rs` shortcuts stay structural.

## What to drop, and where
| Drop | Where | Information cost |
|---|---|---|
| Ghost `PureComponent` | The two ambient merge sites (Phases 3.5 and 3.6) | None. A zero-prop entry plus a spurious `'P'` diagnostic. |
| HTML/DOM attribute props in curated and none mode | Semantic adapter, using the verified `parent` (interface and file) instead of name lists | None. Full mode keeps them, which is what RDT does. |
| `children` without a doc comment | Same adapter | Mirrors RDT's default. I haven't checked what our structural path does. |
| Degrade diagnostics for components tsc resolved | Reconcile step | None; they'd be false. |
| Leaf enrichment, overlay-first design, LSP route, export fields on hints | My earlier plan | None. |
| RDT's JSDoc'd non-components | Already not emitted | Empty props, so nothing lost. |

**Two additions for the compare harness:** compare unions as sets, and emulate RDT's double replace only there and in the RDT projection.

## Not tested
- Static sub-components such as `Menu.Item`.
- Barrel re-exports, where RDT names components by the barrel file.
- Overloads with more than one signature.
- `@type`, `@default` and `visibleName` overrides.
- Any Rust client. All runs used the Node client.
- Large projects.

Two read-only audits (our watch/invalidation and semantic model, and the validation harness metrics) are still running. Their findings on `update_file`, `PropType` variants and how the harness compares will refine the reconcile and freshness sections. I'll fold them in when they land.

Next, I'd write the ADR superseding the leaf-level design and fix the ghost entry, or build the Rust JSON-RPC client against the corpus parity test. Which first?

  Ours is re-rendered TS-side (`run-ours.ts:19-107`, `propTypeToString`), not via Rust `raw_string()` and not via `--format rdt`. Consequences visible in the data:
  - `object` renders as the placeholder `{ ... }` (`:82-84`), whereas Rust `raw_string()` prints real fields.
  - `union` is joined with `' | '` with no parenthesisation of function members (`:70-72`).
  - `literalUnion` is `JSON.stringify(m)` per member (`:97-99`).
  - `eventHandler` renders as `(paramName ?? 'e': eventType) => void` (`:88-90`).
  - `defaultValue` is `prop.defaultValue?.value`, a string of source text.
  
  ### Which per-prop fields are compared (analyze.ts, `comparePair`, lines 124-243)
  - Props are joined by name inside a component. Components are joined by key `${lib}/${basename}/${displayName}` (analyze iterates ours' keys; `:150-158`).
  - Both sides present, checked in this order as an else-if chain (`:196-235`):
    1. `required` strict `!==` gives `required-mismatch`. Type and default are then not checked.
    2. Else `type` strict string `!==`. It is classified by `classifyTypeDiff` (`:59-86`).
       - `cosmetic-formatting` (equal after whitespace collapse and `"` to `'`) counts as matched. Default is not checked in that branch (0 occurrences in the RDT pair).
       - Everything else becomes `type-mismatch` and the default is not checked.
    3. Else `(op.defaultValue ?? null) === (cp.defaultValue ?? null)` (strict) gives matched or `default-mismatch`.
  - `description`, `parent`, `declarations`, and `tags` are never compared by either `analyze.ts` or `compare.ts`.
  - Type buckets (`:34-86`):
    - `cosmetic-formatting`
    - `optional-undefined-representation` (equal after stripping `undefined` members)
    - `union-member-order` (same member multiset, more than 1 member, distinct, different order)
    - `literal-narrowed-vs-widened` (one side is exactly `string|number|boolean|unknown|any` and the other looks literalish)
    - `structural-type-difference` (catch-all)
  - Single-sided props (`:169-192`):
    - Only in ours gives `extra-in-ours`.
    - Only in the comparator gives `missing-in-ours`. It is subdivided into "HTML-inheritance covered" if the name is in our `notableInheritedNames`, else a real miss.
  - `agreementRate = matched / (propsUnion - missingButHtmlInheritanceCovered)` (`:239-240`).
  
  `compare.ts` (older, console-only) is looser:
  - It prints prop-name set differences.
  - It prints a `type diffs` list, only for props in both where both types are non-empty and differ (max 5 shown per component, `:105-122`).
  - It does not compare `required` or `defaultValue`.
  - "Win" = no ours-only, no real RDT-only, no type diffs, and ours has more than 0 props (`:127`).
  - Its `rdtTotal` includes RDT-only bogus components (`:55-63`).

  ## 5. Documented and observed deviations of our RDT-format output
  
  The `--format rdt` serializer is `extract.rs:94-124`. The validate harness does not use it; it uses `--format canonical`.
  
  Documented as intentional:
  - `MIGRATING.md`, "Field-by-field" and "Intentionally omitted":
    - `ref` and `key` omitted.
    - `declarations` is not emitted in `--format rdt` (canonical only; RDT's shape has `declarations`).
    - `methods` is always `[]`.
    - Component `tags` is included although not part of RDT's spec.
    - `parent` is `{name, fileName}`; `fileName` is canonicalized to an absolute path.
    - `defaultValue` is `{value, computed}`.
    - Classes are unsupported.
    - HTML attributes are curated by default (`curated | full | none`); `full` merges the real `@types/react` chain into `props`.
    - NAPI and Vite plugin expose canonical format only.
  - `docs/benchmarks.md:117`: `ref`/`key` are an omission, with no other field holding forwardRef/ref metadata.
  - `docs/benchmarks.md:181` and `.claude/semantic-model/serialization-formats.md` Invariant 4: `composes` is populated with unresolvable-type expressions (mapped/conditional types) as a stop-gap. It mixes react-docgen's own meaning with this repo's.
  - `docs/archive/adversarial-analysis-2026-06-28.md` lines 316-326 ("Design differences vs RDT", D1-D6, point-in-time and historical):
    - D1 HTML expansion
    - D2 literal-union format: says ours is "actual values" vs RDT `enum` (out of date, since `--format rdt` now emits the enum shape)
    - D3 VariantProps `| null`
    - D4 conditional types: opaque here, evaluated in RDT (baseline confirms `derived`: ours conditional text, RDT `"no"`)

content.text:
Both audits are in. I re-checked what I could against the current build, and it moves my recommendation toward something simpler. Anything marked *audit* is a subagent's code reading that I did not execute.

## Verified on the current build
- **Doubled quotes:** the RDT projection emits `enum` values like `""horizontal""` for base-ui `MenuRoot.orientation`. The audit points at `extractor/alias.rs:205` storing already-quoted members that the projection quotes again. I confirmed the symptom, not the cause. This is a bug independent of tsc.
- **Undocumented `children`:** ours emits `children` with an empty description on Badge, Button and Input. RDT's default filter drops these. That explains the 14 extras in the harness.
- **Query order:** across 16 props in 3 files, tsgo's union order was identical with the query order reversed and on a rerun. That is a small sample, not a proof. It still differs from TS 5.9's order.

## What the audits change
1. **Drop hints entirely; run the semantic pass on every file when it's enabled.** *Audit:* silent degradations exist. `Named` fallbacks for utility types and generic parameters, plus `extends` on a TS utility type returning an empty chain, emit no diagnostic. A diagnostic-triggered pass would miss those. It also removes the attribution machinery (`Diagnostic` has no component identity, and line/column are never set). Measured cost was 385 ms for 55 files.
2. **The contract has to live in `crates/core`.** *Audit:* `resolver`, `extractor` and `known` are `pub(crate)`, and `Opaque` can't be built or inspected outside the crate. A backend crate can't patch `Opaque` leaves. Core should define an owned semantic result and merge it internally.
3. **It can't be a `DocgenPlugin`.** *Audit:* the hook is sync, runs only on the cold path, and `update_file` never calls plugins (a documented non-goal).
4. **Watch freshness favours tsc.** *Audit:* our reverse-dependency graph is file-level, built once, and ignores `export *` barrels. Verified last turn: tsc tracks dependencies itself, but only when notified.
5. **The output type can't carry checker types losslessly.** *Audit:* `PropType` has no representation for these cases:
   - Opaque or Named identity
   - handler return types
   - numeric or boolean enum values
   - tuple optional and rest elements
   - index signatures
   - `undefined` members, which are dropped from unions

   I'd add one additive variant holding tsc's exact text plus structure where mappable. There is no schema version field on `ExtractionOutput`, and serde is hand-written (ADR 0002), so that change needs a version bump.
6. **Curated mode gets better.** *Audit:* it currently guesses types by name, and `div` gets a bogus parent `HTMLHTMLAttributes`. With tsgo, take the real props and filter them by the curated names.

## What to drop, and where
| Drop | Where |
|---|---|
| Undocumented `children` | RDT projection only. Canonical keeps it, since it says the component accepts children. |
| `ref` and `key` | Already a documented omission (24 props in the harness). The semantic adapter must apply the same rule so the modes agree. I'd flag that RDT keeps them and nothing else records forwardRef info. |
| HTML/DOM attributes in curated and none mode | Semantic adapter, using the verified `parent`. |
| Ghost `PureComponent` | The two ambient merge sites. |
| Hint attribution, overlay text, leaf replacement, export fields | Gone from the plan. |
| Degrade diagnostics on components tsc resolved | Reconcile step. This is the only reason to keep each component paired with its diagnostics past Phase 5. |

## The measurement harness is confounded
*Audit's recalculation from the on-disk baselines:*
- **Type mismatches:** only 31 of 1,911 are inside the 10 outliers. The `benchmarks.md` sentence saying otherwise isn't supported.
- **Harness rendering:** `run-ours.ts` re-renders our types itself, with `{ ... }` placeholders and event handlers printed as `(e: X) => void`. That accounts for at least some of the 1,344 event-handler mismatches.
- **Fields compared:** it never compares description, parent, declarations or tags, so our current parity on those is unmeasured.
- **Defaults:** the 42 default mismatches are mostly typed values versus source strings (`false` vs `"false"`), which tsc doesn't touch.
- **Version drift:** the docs say RDT 2.2.2, but the lockfile installs 2.4.0.

The tsgo clone works as a fast oracle for description, parent and declarations. Compare unions as sets, and emulate RDT's double replace only in the compare step.

## Not tested
- **Watch-cache staleness:** the audit's dependent-key issues are code reading only.
- **Static sub-components, overloads and barrel re-exports:** overloaded components are rare in the corpus (ariakit `MenuProvider` is the only one, and the extractor has no overload handling).
- **`@default` tag defaults:** whether tsgo supplies the 15 defaults RDT has that we lack.
- **Rust client:** not built.

I'd start with three self-contained fixes: the doubled-quote bug, the ghost entry, and the RDT projection dropping undocumented `children`. Then write the ADR superseding leaf-level enrichment, then build the Rust client against the corpus parity test. Want me to start with the three fixes?

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/gabe/Projects/oxc-react-codegen/.claude/skills/rust-style

**Goal:** Code correct by construction, readable under churn, performant in hot paths.

## Project-specific decisions

These are non-negotiables, not preferences:

- Internal maps: `FxHashMap`. JSON-output maps: `BTreeMap` (deterministic key ordering).
- Type/prop names: `CompactString` — avoids heap allocation for strings ≤24 bytes.
- No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — use `?` and let callers decide what to do with failure.

## Control flow

`let...else` keeps the happy path flat:

```rust
let Some(entry) = map.get(key) else { return None };
let Ok(parsed) = input.parse::<u32>() else { continue };
```

## Matching

No wildcards — a compile error on unhandled variants is a feature:

```rust
match status { Status::Ok => .., Status::Err => .. }  // compiler tells you when Status grows
match status { Status::Ok => .., _ => .. }             // silently misses new variants
```

Full `match` over `matches!` for the same reason.

## Types

Newtypes when a bare type allows confusion. Enums when a bool parameter hides intent:

```rust
struct ScopedKey(CompactString);         // not: String
enum Visibility { Public, Private }      // not: is_public: bool
```

Explicit destructuring gets compiler errors when structs change:

```rust
let ComponentEntry { display_name, file_path, .. } = entry;
```

## Naming

Shadow variables through transformations — no `raw_`/`parsed_`/`trimmed_` prefixes:

```rust
let path = args.path;
let path = path.canonicalize()?;
let path = path.join("config.toml");
```

## Comments

Only when the WHY is non-obvious: a hidden constraint, a workaround, a non-obvious invariant. Not what the code does.

| `required` | ✅ |  |
| `type.name` | ✅ | Literal unions emit `{name: "enum", value: [...]}` matching RDT's convention (so Storybook-style `<select>` controls activate) instead of inlining the literal text |
| `description` | ✅ |  |
| `defaultValue` | ✅ | `{value, computed}` — captured from destructured parameter defaults (`{ variant = 'primary' }`) or JSDoc `@default`, code value wins on conflict |
| `parent.name` / `parent.fileName` | ✅ | `fileName` is always canonicalized to an absolute path regardless of how `--src` was invoked |
| `declarations` | ❌ not emitted in `--format rdt` | Only present in `--format canonical` (the raw internal shape); omitted from both `--format rdt` and `--format storybook` to match RDT's single-parent shape. File an issue if you need it |

### Intentionally omitted

| Prop | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `ref` | Not a user-facing prop — a React internal. RDT includes it because it walks the full inherited type; we treat it as noise |
| `key` | Same reasoning as `ref` |

### HTML attribute inheritance

RDT inlines every inherited HTML attribute (e.g. all ~250-300 members of `ButtonHTMLAttributes`) directly into `props`. This tool doesn't, by default — set `--html-attributes` to control it:

| Mode | Behavior | Reaches `--format rdt` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `curated` (default) | ~15-20 commonly-documented attributes per element (`onClick`, `disabled`, `type`, ARIA attrs) in `notableInherited`. `inheritance` (canonical format only) still records the full layer — element, `Omit`-ted keys. | No |
| `full` | Resolves `@types/react`'s real `HTMLAttributes`/`AriaAttributes`/`DOMAttributes`/`<Element>HTMLAttributes` chain and merges it directly into `props`, matching RDT's flat behavior. | Yes |
| `none` | Own-declared props only. | Yes (nothing to add) |

Flag by layer: `--html-attributes full` (CLI), `htmlAttributes: 'full'` (NAPI), `htmlAttributes: "full"` (`docgen.config.ts`).

content.text:
All three fixes are in and verified. 536 tests pass and rustfmt is clean. Nothing is committed.

## Fixes

| Fix | Before | After (real CLI) |
|---|---|---|
| **Doubled quotes** (`extractor/alias.rs`) | `""horizontal""` | `"horizontal"` |
| **Ghost entry** (`pipeline/mod.rs`, the merge helper for `@types/react` and lib `.d.ts` files) | `PureComponent` plus an unresolvable `'P'` diagnostic | ariakit Full mode gives `Menu`, `MenuButton`, `MenuItem`, `MenuProvider`; 0 `'P'` diagnostics |
| **`children` in RDT output** (`extract.rs`) | Undocumented `children` emitted | Omitted in `--format rdt` when it has no description; canonical keeps it |

## Design choices to check
- **Doubled quotes:** a `null` member now keeps the alias a plain `Union` instead of storing a `"null"` string. `undefined` is dropped from the literal set, as `resolve_union` does. The diagnostic and `composes` text still show quoted members, so AC-10's expected output is unchanged.
- **Ghost entry:** the mappings are dropped only at the merge sites for `@types/react` and lib `.d.ts` files. `.d.ts` files in `src_dirs` still contribute components.
- **`children`:** `MIGRATING.md` has a new row for this.

## The DTS cache
- **Stale cache:** my first snapshot run passed when it shouldn't have. `cache_dir: None` defaults to a persistent `node_modules/.cache/oxc-react-docgen`, which serves parse results by content hash only. So mantine's `.d.ts` came from a pre-fix cache.
- **Schema bump:** I bumped `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` from 3 to 4 and documented why. Without this, existing users would keep the doubled quotes after upgrading.
- **Long term:** the cache should also key on the crate version.

## Tests
- **Written first:** each fix has a failing-first test, and I reverted the fixes to confirm those tests fail without them:
  - 3 extractor tests
  - 1 end-to-end pipeline test (bare members, including template-literal expansion)
  - 2 ghost tests (cold extraction and `WatchSession::initialize`)
  - 1 test on the RDT output
- **Snapshots:** only `snapshot_mantine` changed. I reviewed the diff by hand, since `cargo insta review` is interactive: 4 size sets lost their embedded quotes, and `compact-"xs"` became `compact-xs`. The last one was a hidden effect of the same bug.

## Not caused by me
- `cargo clippy -D warnings` fails on 2 `question_mark` lints in `resolver/template.rs`, which I didn't touch. I left them alone.
- The Storybook projection still emits undocumented `children`. You didn't ask for that one, so I didn't change it.

Ready to commit these, or move on to the ADR that supersedes the leaf-enrichment design?
Anything we should fix before moving on?

Checking the loose ends from this work before answering: consumers of the changed output shape, CI/toolchain for the clippy failure, changeset conventions, working-tree cleanliness, and one resolver bug an audit flagged but I never ran.

Two things are worth doing before moving on. The rest can wait.

## Do now
1. **Add a changeset.** The repo uses `.changeset/*.md`, with a patch bump per crate. This work changes user-visible output:
   - Canonical `literalUnion` members are now bare.
   - `PureComponent` no longer appears in Full mode.
   - RDT output drops undocumented `children`.
   - Everyone's DTS cache resets once.

   Patch versus minor is your call. I'd say patch, since these are bug fixes.
2. **A child interface that redeclares a parent's prop loses to the parent.** I ran `interface Child extends Base { x: "a" | "b" }`. The output has `x: string`, description "base doc" and parent `Base`, where TS and RDT give the child's declaration. The cause is that `merge_parent` skips names already present, and own props are pushed after the merge. So `resolve_component`'s "own props win" comment is wrong. An audit flagged this from code reading, and I've now reproduced it. It affects RDT parity independent of tsc, and it would muddy the semantic reconcile design, so I'd fix it first, with an exact-content test as CLAUDE.md requires.

## Not blockers
- **Clippy:** CI's exact command passes under the pinned Rust 1.96.0. The 2 `template.rs` errors appear only on this machine's 1.98.1. The mise shim tracks `latest`, and mise's 1.96.0 symlink is broken.
- **Harness numbers:**
  - The only TS consumer of literal-union members (`run-ours.ts:98`) is now correct.
  - The harness compares canonical output, so the 14 `children` extras stay until it applies the same filter.
  - `docs/benchmarks.md` (2026-07-25) predates HEAD and needs regenerating.
- **DTS cache:** it invalidates only on the schema number, which is what bit us today. Keying it on the crate version too would prevent that. Follow-up.
- **Storybook output** still emits undocumented `children`, unchanged.
- **Doc drift:** I found no docs that assert the old quoted-member contract (a keyword grep, not exhaustive). Your uncommitted `type-checker-integration.md` and ADR 0004 edits still describe the leaf model.

# callisto configuration
#
# Mirrors ~/projects/michi's proven callisto.toml shape — the closest
# existing reference for a Rust-crates + NAPI-binding + npm-wrapper
# monorepo. One structural difference from michi: michi's NAPI crate and
# its npm wrapper share a single directory (packages/michi-node/, holding
# both Cargo.toml and package.json), whereas this repo splits them across
# crates/binding (the cdylib) and packages/napi (the npm wrapper) — expressed
# as two separate [[package]] entries joined by a [[fixed-group]] below, the
# same mechanism michi uses for its own crate+wrapper pair.
#
# `[[package]] match` is a PACKAGE NAME (bare, or "<ecosystem>/<name>"
# ecosystem-qualified — one of cargo/npm/pypi/go/maven/nuget/deno/jsr),
# never a directory path — confirmed against callisto-model's PackageId::parse
# and callisto-graph's own test suite (crates/callisto-graph/src/config/
# resolve.rs, tests/per_package_config_test.rs). A directory-path `match`
# (e.g. "crates/core") parses to a literal bare name that no real package is
# ever named, so the rule silently matches nothing — verified empirically:
# an earlier draft of this file used directory paths for every [[package]]
# entry and callisto plan-publish still listed crates/binding for a cratesIo
# publish despite publish-to = [] below, because that override was never
# actually being applied. michi's own callisto.toml has this same mistake
# (match = "packages/michi-node", match = "."), which is presumably why it
# went unnoticed there too — its manifest-derived defaults happen to already
# match what it wants.
#
# Pinned to callisto 0.8.0 (GitHub Release `callisto@0.8.0`, commit
# c5578e6a63754b54575b3ac7518cc1753e443393). .github/workflows/release.yml
# pins both callisto actions to that commit and installs the attested
# prebuilt CLI with `verification: require`.
#
# 0.8 split releasing into two authority boundaries: callisto-action only
# creates or updates the `callisto/version-packages` PR — its former
# `publish` input no longer exists — and publication runs from the merged
# release commit through `callisto release plan` → `callisto release execute`
# in this repo's own durable workflow. That path reads the `publish-to`
# overrides below as authority, unlike the legacy `callisto plan-publish`
# command this file was originally written against.
#
# 0.8 also adds a `[release]` section for product binary assets, deliberately
# unused here: its `artifact-targets` are validated against callisto's own
# hardcoded (target, asset-name) table (`PRODUCT_ARTIFACT_TARGETS`), so no
# other workspace can declare it. With no `[release]` section the derived
# intent carries no artifact slots, which release.yml asserts before
# executing.
#
# No .moon/workspace.yml changes are needed: the moon WASM extension
# (crates/callisto-moon) only implements read-only `status`/`plan-publish`
# reporting subcommands — no `publish`/`tag`/apply path exists through it.
# setup-callisto puts the `callisto` binary on $GITHUB_PATH directly; moon is
# installed alongside it as a toolchain dependency, not as callisto's host.

# Group members and changeset frontmatter resolve bare names through
# callisto's identity index, which errors on an ambiguous name rather than
# guessing. The private root package.json is therefore named
# `oxc-react-docgen-workspace`, not `oxc-react-docgen`: sharing the CLI
# crate's name made every `oxc-react-docgen: patch` changeset ambiguous
# across cargo and npm. The fixed-group members below stay ecosystem-
# qualified anyway, since that is cheap insurance against the same collision.

[changesets]
dir = ".changeset"

[cascade]
mode = "out-of-range"
bump-severity = "patch"
peer-escalation = true
preserve-npm-ranges = true

# Rust library crate — published to crates.io, no npm counterpart. Consumed
# via path dependency by both crates/cli and crates/binding.
[[package]]
match = "cargo/oxc-react-docgen-core"
publish-to = ["crates-io"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# Rust CLI crate — published to crates.io. packages/cli wraps its compiled
# per-platform binaries for npm distribution; kept in lockstep below.
[[package]]
match = "cargo/oxc-react-docgen"
publish-to = ["crates-io"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# npm CLI wrapper — distributes crates/cli's compiled binaries.
[[package]]
match = "npm/@oxc-react-docgen/cli"
publish-to = ["npm"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# NAPI binding crate (cdylib) — not published to crates.io independently (no
# real-world use case for `cargo add`ing an FFI shim on its own). Callisto
# still tracks/bumps its version to stay in lockstep with its npm wrapper via
# the fixed-group below, but is excluded from the crates.io publish plan.
#
# Under 0.8's release path this override is authoritative: intent derivation
# builds registry-publish operations (and the tag that depends on them)
# straight from `publish-to`, so an empty list yields neither a crates.io
# publish nor a tag for this crate. crates/binding/Cargo.toml's own
# `publish = false` remains the second gate — callisto-manifests'
# is_publishable() still treats a missing `publish` key as true, which is
# what the legacy `callisto plan-publish` command reads.
[[package]]
match = "cargo/oxc-react-docgen-napi"
publish-to = []
release-trigger = "changeset"

# npm NAPI wrapper — distributes crates/binding's compiled .node binaries.
[[package]]
match = "npm/@oxc-react-docgen/napi"
publish-to = ["npm"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# Vite plugin — standalone npm package, no Rust counterpart.
[[package]]
match = "npm/@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin"
publish-to = ["npm"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# Keep the NAPI binding crate and its npm wrapper versioned in lockstep —
# the npm package is meaningless without a matching binding build.
[[fixed-group]]
name = "napi-and-binding"
members = ["cargo/oxc-react-docgen-napi", "npm/@oxc-react-docgen/napi"]

# Keep the CLI crate and its npm wrapper versioned in lockstep — the npm
# package just redistributes this crate's compiled binaries.
[[fixed-group]]
name = "cli-and-npm-wrapper"
members = ["cargo/oxc-react-docgen", "npm/@oxc-react-docgen/cli"]

=== literal-union-bare-members
---
oxc-react-docgen-core: patch
---

String-literal union aliases now report bare member values. A `type Size = "sm" | "md"` alias previously came back with each member already quoted, so serialized output showed `""sm"" | ""md""` and a template literal over the alias expanded to `compact-"sm"`. `undefined` members are dropped (optionality is reported through `required`); a `null` member keeps the alias a plain union, since a string-only literal union can't represent it.

The DTS cache schema version moved to 4 — its key is a content hash and can't detect that the extractor now produces different data for identical input, so existing cache files are discarded rather than served stale.
=== ambient-dts-types-not-components
---
oxc-react-docgen-core: patch
---

Ambient `.d.ts` files are merged for their types only, never their components. `@types/react` declares `class PureComponent<P, S, SS> extends Component<P, S, SS>`, which matched the class-component detector — full HTML-attribute mode emitted `PureComponent` as a 0-prop component alongside a `Cannot resolve type 'P'` diagnostic. Both are gone, from batch extraction and from the watch session's first revision.
=== rdt-skip-undocumented-children
---
oxc-react-docgen: patch
---

`--format rdt` omits a `children` prop that has no description, matching react-docgen-typescript's default `skipChildrenPropWithoutDoc`. A documented `children` is still emitted, and `--format canonical` is unchanged.

p = 'crates/core/src/resolver/chain.rs'

    let parent = PropParent { name: iface.name.to_string(), file_name: iface.file_path.to_string() };

new = '''    // ── Resolve own props ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // A redeclared prop replaces the inherited one, as in TS; `resolve_component` keeps the first duplicate it sees.
    let own_names: FxHashSet<&str> = iface.props.iter().map(|prop| prop.name.as_str()).collect();
    chain.props.retain(|prop| !own_names.contains(prop.name.as_str()));

    let parent = PropParent { name: iface.name.to_string(), file_name: iface.file_path.to_string() };
'''
assert old in s
open(p, 'w').write(s.replace(old, new, 1))
EOF

# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install Cargo tools required for local development
install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest --locked
    cargo install cargo-llvm-cov --locked
    cargo install cargo-machete --locked
    cargo install cargo-mutants --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Check the public Rust API for accidental SemVer breaks against the last
# published version. Not wired into `just ci` yet — there is no published
# baseline to diff against until v0.1.0's first real crates.io release ships.
# Install with `cargo install cargo-semver-checks --locked` once needed.
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

# Install all dependencies
install:
    pnpm install
    cargo fetch

# Build all projects. Rust crates build via one workspace-wide cargo
# invocation, not `moon run :build` — that fans out one `cargo build -p`
# per crate, and every one of those processes contends for the same
# target/ file lock, serializing what moon's own scheduler thinks is
# parallel work (confirmed via `Blocking waiting for file lock` in verbose
# output). napi/vite-plugin have no such lock to contend over, so moon
# still orchestrates those directly.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi
    moon run napi:build vite-plugin:build
    cargo build --release

# Run Rust unit tests (via nextest, which doesn't run doctests — paired
# with `cargo test --doc` to cover those too)
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

# Run TypeScript tests
test-ts:
    pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin test

# Run all tests (Rust + TypeScript)
test-all: test test-ts

# Run benchmarks
bench:
    cargo bench --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

# Coverage report — opens HTML in browser
coverage:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked --html --open

# Documentation build check (warnings, including broken intra-doc links,
# treated as errors)
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

# Unused-dependency check
machete:
    cargo machete

# Mutation testing sweep — slow, run on demand, not part of `just ci`
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

ts_src := "'packages/vite-plugin/src/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/tests/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/validate/src/**/*.ts'"
ts_src_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/src' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/validate/src'"
ts_tests_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/tests'"
md_src := "'**/*.md' '!node_modules/**' '!target/**' '!dist/**'"

# Lint and format check
lint:
    cargo fmt --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked -- -D warnings
    pnpm exec oxfmt --check {{ts_src}}
    pnpm exec oxfmt --check {{md_src}}
    pnpm exec oxlint {{ts_src_only}}
    pnpm exec oxlint -A pedantic -A perf -A style -A unicorn/consistent-function-scoping -A vitest/require-mock-type-parameters --vitest-plugin {{ts_tests_only}}

# Format code
fmt:
    cargo fmt
    pnpm exec oxfmt {{ts_src}}
    pnpm exec oxfmt {{md_src}}

# Check licenses, advisories, and banned crates
deny:
    cargo deny check

# Check for typos
typos:
    typos

# Lint GitHub Actions workflows for permission, credential, and supply-chain
# issues. --strict-collection fails on a workflow it cannot parse instead of
# skipping it, so a malformed file can never pass by being ignored.
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Everything the moon-managed pre-commit hook runs. `.moon/workspace.yml`
# calls this recipe rather than repeating the commands, so the hook and
# `just ci` can't drift apart.
pre-commit:
    cargo fmt --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked -- -D warnings
    typos
    cargo deny check

# Simulate full CI locally (lint → test → deny → typos → zizmor → doc-check → machete → ts tests)
ci: lint test deny typos zizmor doc-check machete test-ts

# Run moon compare task (accuracy vs react-docgen + react-docgen-typescript)
compare:
    moon run validate:compare

# Clean build artifacts
clean:
    moon clean
    cargo clean
    rm -rf node_modules

# Setup toolchain via proto
setup:
    proto install
    pnpm install
    moon sync vcs-hooks

# Run moon commands
moon *args:
    moon {{args}}

# Run cargo commands
cargo *args:
    cargo {{args}}

Both tasks are done, and I have a CI proposal for you to decide on.

## The two fixes

**1. Changeset.** Your session had already committed my three fixes with changesets (`e7b6289`, `1d7301a`, `d3e544a`), so there was nothing to add.

**2. Redeclared props.** A child interface's redeclaration now replaces the parent's. The change is in `resolve_interface_chain`, and the new test is `child_interface_redeclaring_a_prop_wins_over_every_ancestor`.

- **What I checked against RDT:** running real RDT on an override fixture showed an undocumented override inherits only the description. Tags and `@default` don't inherit, and a documented override wins outright. A naive fix would have dropped `mui/TextField.InputProps`'s description.
- **Snapshots:**
  - Only 6 props changed, in chakra and mui.

  - Parent and description match RDT on all 6.
- **Changeset:** `.changeset/child-interface-prop-overrides-parent.md`.
- **CI gates:** fmt is clean, CI's exact clippy command passes, and 544 tests pass. Nothing is committed.

## CI

- **Where it differs from callisto and michi:**
  - Callisto's own CI ends with a `validate` job (`callisto validate`) that checks changesets and simulates the publish plan. Ours never validates changesets.
  - Callisto's jobs are thin and call `just` recipes. Ours repeat the commands, and they've already drifted: `just ci` runs `typos`, CI doesn't.
  - Callisto's `validate` job depends on all the others, so it serves as one stable required check.
  - michi's 160-line flat CI is the better shape to copy. Callisto's own CI is 231 lines because of release-artifact matrices we don't need.
- **Where ours is complicated:**
  - **`ci.yml` size:** it is 393 lines with 11 jobs, 57 of them comment lines.
  - **`detect-changes`:** this job alone is about 80 lines of moon, python and shell that skip jobs on some PRs. `actionlint` flags shellcheck issues in it, and neither reference repo has anything like it.
  - **Job setup:** each job also repeats a `contents: read` block, and `hygiene` duplicates `lint`'s setup.
  - **Extra jobs:** `bench` runs full benchmarks on main and uploads a text file, and `coverage` reruns the whole test suite.
  - **`install` job:** it carries 45 lines of inline shell.
  - **Toolchain pin:** it lives in both `.prototools` and `ci.yml`. They match today, but the file comments say to keep them in lockstep.

## Proposed shape
About 110 lines, 5 jobs, each calling a `just` recipe.

- **Recipes:** split `just lint` into Rust and TS halves, and move the install check into a script.
- **Permissions:** set `permissions: contents: read` once at the top.
- **Additions:** add `typos` and `callisto validate`.
- **Pin:** read the toolchain pin from `.prototools`.
- **Aggregate job:** finish with one job that depends on the rest.
- **Removals:** drop `detect-changes`, the `bench` job and every comment that only explains history.
- **Verification:** `actionlint` and `zizmor` are installed locally, so I can check syntax and security before pushing. I can't run the workflow itself here.

Two questions before I rewrite it:
1. Are you fine with Rust jobs running on TS-only PRs? Cached, that costs little.
2. Is codecov actually wired up? If not, I'd drop `coverage` rather than keep a non-blocking duplicate test run.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Installs the packed vite-plugin into an empty project and checks @oxc-react-docgen/napi arrives only as its
# transitive dependency. Usage: scripts/verify-install.sh <npm|pnpm>
set -euo pipefail

pm=${1:?usage: verify-install.sh <npm|pnpm>}
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

packed=$(mktemp -d)
project=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$packed" "$project"' EXIT

pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin build
pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/napi --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin pack --pack-destination "$packed"

# proto resolves pnpm from .prototools, which the temp project sits outside of.
PROTO_PNPM_VERSION=$(pnpm --version)
export PROTO_PNPM_VERSION

napi=$(ls "$packed"/oxc-react-docgen-napi-*.tgz)
plugin=$(ls "$packed"/oxc-react-docgen-vite-plugin-*.tgz)

# The override serves napi from this checkout's tarball instead of the registry. pnpm 11 reads overrides from
# pnpm-workspace.yaml, not package.json.
cd "$project"
if [ "$pm" = npm ]; then
  printf '{"private":true,"overrides":{"@oxc-react-docgen/napi":"file:%s"}}\n' "$napi" > package.json
  npm install "$plugin"
else
  echo '{"private":true}' > package.json
  printf 'overrides:\n  "@oxc-react-docgen/napi": "file:%s"\n' "$napi" > pnpm-workspace.yaml
  pnpm add "$plugin"
fi

# Resolve napi from vite-plugin's own location: pnpm doesn't hoist transitive deps into node_modules/, and the
# plugin's `exports` has only an `import` condition, so `require.resolve` can't reach it from here.
node --input-type=module <<'EOF'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';

const { dependencies = {} } = JSON.parse(readFileSync('package.json', 'utf8'));
if (dependencies['@oxc-react-docgen/napi']) {
  throw new Error('napi is a direct dependency; the check proves nothing');
}
const plugin = import.meta.resolve('@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin');
createRequire(plugin).resolve('@oxc-react-docgen/napi/package.json');
console.log('OK');
EOF

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1

# Each job runs `just` recipes, so `just ci` locally does what CI does.
jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:

      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@94c31af3204a9f15ab40b35ad084410b905bbc73 # v2.87.17

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:

          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1

      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@94c31af3204a9f15ab40b35ad084410b905bbc73 # v2.87.17

      # The cli config tests spawn `node --import=tsx/esm`, and tsx is a devDependency of apps/validate.
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0.6.4

      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-pnpm-cache@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: just test

  ts:
    name: TypeScript / Node ${{ matrix.node }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node: ["24", "26"]
    env:
      PROTO_NODE_VERSION: ${{ matrix.node }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:

      - run: just test-ts

  install:
    name: Install / Node ${{ matrix.node }} / ${{ matrix.pm }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

        node: ["24", "26"]
        pm: [npm, pnpm]
    env:
      PROTO_NODE_VERSION: ${{ matrix.node }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:

      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@94c31af3204a9f15ab40b35ad084410b905bbc73 # v2.87.17

      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0.6.4

      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-pnpm-cache@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:

          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-validate@c5578e6a63754b54575b3ac7518cc1753e443393 # callisto@0.8.0

  # The one check to require in branch protection.
  ci:
    name: CI
    needs: [lint, test, ts, install, audit, changesets]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - if: contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') || contains(needs.*.result, 'cancelled')
        run: exit 1

CI is rewritten and every command in it passes locally, but it hasn't run on GitHub yet. `ci.yml` went from 393 lines and 11 jobs to 145 lines and 7 (6 checks plus one aggregate). Comment lines went from 57 to 3.

## New CI
Each job runs `just` recipes, so `just ci` locally now does what CI does.

| Job | Runs |
|---|---|
| Lint | `just lint doc-check machete typos` (now includes `typos`, which CI was missing) |
| Test | `just test` |
| TypeScript / Node 24, 26 | `just test-ts` |
| Install / Node × npm, pnpm | `just verify-install <pm>` |
| Audit | `just deny zizmor` |
| Changesets | `callisto-validate`, pinned to the same 0.8.0 commit as `release.yml` |
| CI | aggregate job that fails if any of the above failed |

The toolchain version is now read from `.prototools`, so it has one source. The other changes:

- **Removed:** the `detect-changes` job, the full-benchmark job (`just bench` remains), and the coverage job. I found no codecov config or mention anywhere, and `just coverage` remains.
- **Moved:** the 45 lines of inline install-check shell are now `scripts/verify-install.sh`.
- **Added:** a `verify-install` recipe in the justfile.
